entities.name: Please list all the superpowers of 3-D Man.

properties.sql:
SELECT sp.power_name
FROM superhero AS s
JOIN hero_power AS hp ON s.id = hp.hero_id
JOIN superpower AS sp ON hp.power_id = sp.id
WHERE s.superhero_name = '3-D Man'

entities.name: How many superheroes have the super power of "Super Strength"?

FROM hero_power AS hp
INNER JOIN superpower AS sp ON hp.power_id = sp.id
WHERE sp.power_name = 'Super Strength'

entities.name: Among the superheroes with the super power of "Super Strength", how many of them have a height of over 200cm?

properties.note: Speed is stored as a named attribute, so the slowest hero is the one whose hero_attribute.attribute_value for attribute.attribute_name = 'Speed' is lowest.
properties.sql: hero_attribute.attribute_value

properties.note: In this database a superhero's weight is considered missing when weight_kg is NULL or stored as 0, so both cases must be filtered.
properties.sql: superhero.weight_kg IS NULL OR superhero.weight_kg = 0

properties.note: Eye color is stored as a foreign key superhero.eye_colour_id into the colour lookup table, whose colour.colour holds the literal color name.
properties.sql: superhero.eye_colour_id = colour.id AND colour.colour = 'Brown'

properties.note: Superheroes sharing an identical full_name are treated as one person when aggregating, so counts are grouped by superhero.full_name rather than by superhero.id, and the output list uses DISTINCT superhero.full_name.
properties.sql: superhero.full_name

properties.note: Compute a percentage as the conditional count of the subset multiplied by 100 divided by the total row count of the same filtered population, counting superhero.id in both numerator and denominator so the denominator is unaffected by the case expression.
properties.sql: CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN colour.colour = 'Blue' THEN superhero.id ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(superhero.id)

properties.note: Gender is stored as a lookup label in gender.gender ('Female', 'Male', 'N/A'), reached via superhero.gender_id.
properties.sql: superhero.gender_id = gender.id AND gender.gender = 'Female'

properties.note: When a question states a superhero's colour without specifying eye/hair, it refers to the skin colour attribute, so join colour through superhero.skin_colour_id, not superhero.eye_colour_id.
properties.sql: superhero.skin_colour_id = colour.id AND colour.colour = 'Blue'

properties.note: Height is stored in centimeters and a height of NULL or 0 means the superhero's height is unknown rather than zero tall.
properties.sql: superhero.height_cm IS NULL OR superhero.height_cm = 0

properties.note: When aggregating per superhero (e.g. ranking heroes by a count), group by superhero.superhero_name so the grouping unit matches the named superhero entity.
properties.sql: superhero.superhero_name

properties.note: The superhero trait 'Speed' is a row in attribute with attribute_name = 'Speed', whose per-hero value lives in hero_attribute.attribute_value.
properties.sql: attribute.attribute_name = 'Speed'

properties.note: An individual superhero is identified by superhero.id, so grouping or joining per superhero keys off that id rather than the (possibly non-unique) superhero_name.
properties.sql: superhero.id

properties.note: Average height here is a single overall average across all superhero rows, computed as total height divided by the number of superheroes, so it must not be split by superhero_name.
properties.sql: CAST(SUM(superhero.height_cm) AS REAL) / COUNT(superhero.id)

properties.note: The publisher of a hero is stored as an id in superhero.publisher_id that resolves to the name in publisher.publisher_name.
properties.sql: publisher.publisher_name

properties.note: superhero.full_name can be NULL, so name listings should exclude NULL names.
properties.sql: superhero.full_name IS NOT NULL

properties.note: Eye color is stored as a foreign key superhero.eye_colour_id into the colour lookup table, whose colour.colour holds the literal color name.
properties.sql: superhero.eye_colour_id = colour.id AND colour.colour = 'Brown'

properties.note: Weight is stored in kilograms in superhero.weight_kg, where 0 or NULL means the weight is unknown rather than an actual measurement.
properties.sql: superhero.weight_kg

properties.note: The id of the superhero owning an attribute row is hero_attribute.hero_id, which maps to superhero(id).
properties.sql: hero_attribute.hero_id

properties.note: When a question states a superhero's colour without specifying eye/hair, it refers to the skin colour attribute, so join colour through superhero.skin_colour_id, not superhero.eye_colour_id.
properties.sql: superhero.skin_colour_id = colour.id AND colour.colour = 'Blue'

properties.note: A hero's publisher is found by joining superhero.publisher_id to publisher.id and returning publisher.publisher_name.
properties.sql: superhero.publisher_id

properties.note: The literal '-' stored in superhero.full_name is a real stored value and is counted as having a name, so it must be excluded explicitly only when counting superheroes that do have a full name.
properties.sql: superhero.full_name <> '-'

properties.note: A superhero belongs to a publisher through superhero.publisher_id -> publisher.id, and the publisher's business name is publisher.publisher_name (values like 'DC Comics' and 'Marvel Comics').
properties.sql: superhero.publisher_id = publisher.id AND publisher.publisher_name = 'DC Comics'

properties.note: When a question phrases a capability as the hero's "power", the name is stored in superpower.power_name and linked to heroes through hero_power.power_id = superpower.id.
properties.sql: superpower.power_name

properties.note: Compute a percentage as the conditional count of the subset multiplied by 100 divided by the total row count of the same filtered population, counting superhero.id in both numerator and denominator so the denominator is unaffected by the case expression.
properties.sql: CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN colour.colour = 'Blue' THEN superhero.id ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(superhero.id)

properties.note: For a 'percentage of group A that are B' question, the population (female heroes) goes in WHERE while the subset of interest (Marvel Comics) is tested inside the conditional count divided by the full population count.
properties.sql: CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN publisher.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN 1 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(superhero.id)

properties.note: A superhero's publishing company is found by matching superhero.publisher_id to publisher.id and reading publisher.publisher_name.
properties.sql: superhero.publisher_id = publisher.id

properties.note: In the colour table the 'No Colour' row has id = 1, so superheroes whose skin_colour_id is 1 are the ones with no skin colour.
properties.sql: superhero.skin_colour_id = 1

properties.note: superhero.full_name holds the person's full name but may be NULL or the placeholder '-'; when listing superheroes by name, return the stored value as-is rather than filtering out NULLs/placeholders or de-duplicating names.
properties.sql: superhero.full_name

properties.note: Gender is stored as a lookup label in gender.gender ('Female', 'Male', 'N/A'), reached via superhero.gender_id.
properties.sql: superhero.gender_id = gender.id AND gender.gender = 'Female'

properties.note: Eye color is stored as a foreign key superhero.eye_colour_id into the colour lookup table, whose colour.colour holds the literal color name.
properties.sql: superhero.eye_colour_id = colour.id AND colour.colour = 'Brown'

properties.note: A superhero belongs to a publisher through superhero.publisher_id -> publisher.id, and the publisher's business name is publisher.publisher_name (values like 'DC Comics' and 'Marvel Comics').
properties.sql: superhero.publisher_id = publisher.id AND publisher.publisher_name = 'DC Comics'

properties.note: A superhero belongs to a publisher through superhero.publisher_id -> publisher.id, and the publisher's business name is publisher.publisher_name (values like 'DC Comics' and 'Marvel Comics').
properties.sql: superhero.publisher_id = publisher.id AND publisher.publisher_name = 'DC Comics'

properties.note: This 'average' is a count-based ratio: total superheroes divided by the number of superheroes in the specified skin-colour group, not an average of an attribute such as height_cm.
properties.sql: CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN superhero.skin_colour_id = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)

properties.note: Gender is stored as a text label in gender.gender ('Female', 'Male', 'N/A') and must be looked up through superhero.gender_id = gender.id.
properties.sql: gender.gender = 'Female'

properties.note: The number of powers held by a superhero is the number of hero_power association rows for that hero, so count hero_power.hero_id (always populated on a matched row) rather than hero_power.power_id, which can be NULL on some rows and undercount.
properties.sql: COUNT(hero_power.hero_id)

properties.note: A superhero's numeric skill/power rating for one attribute is stored in hero_attribute.attribute_value, where larger numbers mean more skilled or powerful in that area.
properties.sql: hero_attribute.attribute_value

properties.note: For a 'percentage of group A that are B' question, the population (female heroes) goes in WHERE while the subset of interest (Marvel Comics) is tested inside the conditional count divided by the full population count.
properties.sql: CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN publisher.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN 1 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(superhero.id)

properties.note: Eye color is stored in the shared colour table and reached from a superhero via superhero.eye_colour_id = colour.id, so the text value is colour.colour.
properties.sql: colour.colour

properties.note: In this database the phrase describing heroes who act for their own benefit or by their own moral code is stored as the alignment category 'Bad', not 'Neutral'.
properties.sql: alignment.alignment = 'Bad'

properties.note: A superhero's publisher is identified by publisher.publisher_name (full names such as 'Marvel Comics') joined through superhero.publisher_id = publisher.id.
properties.sql: publisher.publisher_name

properties.note: When a question states a superhero's colour without specifying eye/hair, it refers to the skin colour attribute, so join colour through superhero.skin_colour_id, not superhero.eye_colour_id.
properties.sql: superhero.skin_colour_id = colour.id AND colour.colour = 'Blue'

properties.note: Popularity of a color is the number of superheroes having that color, so aggregate COUNT(superhero.id) grouped by colour.colour and rank in descending count order.
properties.sql: RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(superhero.id) DESC)

properties.note: A superhero 'without a full name' is a row whose superhero.full_name is SQL NULL; no trimming or other value checks are applied.
properties.sql: superhero.full_name IS NULL

properties.note: A hero's powers are the rows in hero_power linked by hero_power.hero_id, so the count of a hero's powers is COUNT(hero_power.power_id) over that hero's rows.
properties.sql: COUNT(hero_power.power_id)

properties.note: Gender is stored as a lookup label in gender.gender ('Female', 'Male', 'N/A'), reached via superhero.gender_id.
properties.sql: superhero.gender_id = gender.id AND gender.gender = 'Female'

properties.note: Heroes with no publisher are stored with publisher_id = 1, the placeholder entry in the publisher table, rather than with a NULL publisher_id.
properties.sql: superhero.publisher_id = 1

properties.note: Counting superheroes means counting superhero.id values (one row per hero), not publisher rows.
properties.sql: COUNT(superhero.id)

properties.note: A superhero's publishing company is found by matching superhero.publisher_id to publisher.id and reading publisher.publisher_name.
properties.sql: superhero.publisher_id = publisher.id

properties.note: Average height here is a single overall average across all superhero rows, computed as total height divided by the number of superheroes, so it must not be split by superhero_name.
properties.sql: CAST(SUM(superhero.height_cm) AS REAL) / COUNT(superhero.id)

properties.note: A difference in counts is a signed subtraction of the two category counts (first minus second), not the absolute value, and it must not be returned alongside a separately picked 'top' publisher name.
properties.sql: SUM(CASE WHEN publisher.publisher_name = 'DC Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN publisher.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
